source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Choose correctly between rotation, revolution, and satellite motion when describing how Earth, planets, and moons move.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Earth's turning about its axis is revolution.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: An artificial spacecraft orbiting Earth is not a satellite.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: The Moon revolves around the Sun instead of around Earth.

intelligence.enrichment: Rotation is turning about an axis, while revolution is the movement of an object around another object; planets revolve around the Sun, and satellites such as moons move around planets. The path relation decides the word: spinning on an axis is rotation, moving around another body is revolution, and moving around a planet identifies a satellite relation. The learner correctly applies this rule: Rotation is turning about an axis, while revolution is the movement of an object around another object; planets revolve around the Sun, and satellites such as moons move around planets. All movement in space is called rotation, whether an object spins or goes around another object.
